end.summary:
Practised identifying standing, sleeping and slanting straight lines.
Named straight and curved lines in letters and familiar objects.
Identified line types in T, L, H, A and HAT.
Recognised a bangle and circle as curved; triangle was discussed as straight-sided.
Teach-back was not passed; 6 of 7 line-identification attempts were unaided correct.
end.parentNote: Om practised standing, sleeping, slanting, straight and curved lines using letters and everyday objects. They used examples such as a flagpole, slide, bangle, circle and triangle, and identified the three line types in HAT. There was some uncertainty about whether a bent-looking V or triangle could be curved; this was discussed, but the triangle point was not fully settled by the end. At home, ask Om to find and name one example of each line type in a room or on a page.
